recipes.name: Fried Bear inspired Food Wars!
ingredients: 3 lbs bear ribs and bear kebab meat (sirloin cut)
2 lbs bear New York steak (or a similar cut), pounded
2 lbs bear short rib and brisket, cut into chunks
1 tsp ground schisandra berries (or substitute with a mix of tart dried fruit)
3 cups bear stock, reduced to 1 cup
3 tbsp Amur Cork tree honey (or another bitter honey)
instructions: For the Bear Stock
Preheat your oven to 450°F.
Cut the bear ribs and kebab meat into chunks and roast in the oven for 30 minutes until golden brown. - 3 lbs bear ribs and bear kebab meat (sirloin cut)

Transfer the roasted bear bones and meat into a large pot. Add the chopped onions, carrots, garlic, ginger slices, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Cover with water and bring to a simmer. - 3 lbs bear ribs and bear kebab meat (sirloin cut) - 2 onions cut into chunks - 3 large carrots roughly chopped - 1 head garlic halved - 3 ½ slices of ginger - 1 tbsp black peppercorns - 2 bay leaves - Water (enough to cover everything)
Let simmer for about 4 hours until the meat is tender and the flavors have melded.
Strain the stock, pressing down on the solids to extract all the juices. Set aside.
For the Marinade

In a food processor, combine the onion chunks, garlic, ginger, kosher salt, and black pepper. Blend into a smooth puree. - 1 white onion cut into chunks - 8 cloves garlic - 3 slices ginger - 1 tsp kosher salt - 1 tsp black pepper
Pound the bear steaks with a meat mallet until tender, using plastic wrap to prevent tearing. - 2 lbs bear New York steak (or a similar cut) pounded
Rub the puree onto the steaks, making sure they are well coated. Let the steaks marinate in the fridge for at least 24 hours. - 2 lbs bear New York steak (or a similar cut) pounded
For the Cajun Spice Mix

Combine all the Cajun spice mix ingredients in a small bowl and mix with a whisk. Set aside. - 1 tbsp paprika - 2 tsp garlic powder - 2 tsp kosher salt - 1 tsp onion powder - 1 tsp freshly ground black pepper - 1 tsp dried oregano - 1 tsp dried thyme - ½ tsp cayenne pepper
For the Bear Gravy
Render the bear fat in a small saucepan over medium heat. Once melted, whisk in the flour to make a roux. Cook until the roux turns golden brown. - 3 tbsp bear fat (from trimmings) - 3 tbsp flour
Slowly whisk in ½ cup of bear stock, followed by the milk, continuing to whisk to avoid lumps. - For the Bear Stock - 1 cup milk
Season with Cajun spice blend, juniper berries, and salt. Cook until thickened, then set aside. - For the Cajun Spice Mix - Juniper berries crushed (to taste) - Salt (to taste)
For the Chicken-Fried Bear
After the bear steaks have marinated, remove them from the marinade and pat them dry. - 2 lbs bear New York steak (or a similar cut) pounded
Mix together ¼ cup flour and 2 tsp Cajun spice blend. Beat two eggs with a splash of water for the batter. - Flour (for dredging) - 2 eggs beaten - For the Cajun Spice Mix
Heat oil to 350°F in a large frying pan or deep fryer. - Oil for frying
Dip the bear steak chunks into the flour mixture, then into the egg batter, and fry in the hot oil until golden brown and crispy (about 3-5 minutes). - For the Chicken Fried Bear - For the Breading
Drain on a wire rack and serve with the bear gravy. - For the Bear Gravy
For the Schisandra Berry Sauce
In a saucepan, reduce the 3 cups of bear stock down to 1 cup over medium heat. - For the Bear Stock - 3 cups bear stock reduced to 1 cup
In another pan, sauté the onions and garlic in butter until golden brown. - 1 medium onion diced - 4 cloves garlic minced - 3 tbsp butter

In a third pan, caramelize the Amur Cork tree honey until slightly bitter. Add balsamic vinegar to deglaze and balance the sweetness. - 3 tbsp Amur Cork tree honey (or another bitter honey) - 3 tbsp balsamic vinegar

Combine the reduced stock, sautéed onions, garlic, and honey mixture in a single vessel. Blend with an immersion blender for a smooth consistency. - 3 cups bear stock reduced to 1 cup - 1 medium onion diced - 4 cloves garlic minced - 3 tbsp Amur Cork tree honey (or another bitter honey)
Add in the sake-steeped schisandra berries and season with salt. - 2 tbsp sake steeped schisandra berries - Salt to taste
For the Menchi Katsu
Use a food processor or meat grinder to grind the chilled bear short rib and brisket into ground meat. - 2 lbs bear short rib and brisket cut into chunks

Mix the ground bear with sautéed onions, an egg, panko breadcrumbs, schisandra berries, and a splash of bear stock. - Panko breadcrumbs - 1 medium onion diced - 1 tsp ground schisandra berries (or substitute with a mix of tart dried fruit) - 4 tbsp panko breadcrumbs - 1 tbsp bear stock - 1 egg
Shape the mixture into burger-sized patties. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to firm up.
Set up a breading station: flour, beaten eggs, and panko breadcrumbs. - Flour (for dredging) - 2 eggs beaten - Panko breadcrumbs
Coat each patty in flour, dip in egg, and coat in panko breadcrumbs. - Flour (for dredging) - 2 eggs beaten - Panko breadcrumbs
Fry in 350°F oil for a few minutes until golden brown and crispy. Drain on a wire rack. - Oil for frying
For the Chicken-Fried Bear, serve the fried bear cutlets with lettuce and a ramekin of bear gravy on the side. - For the Bear Gravy
For the Bear Menchi Katsu, drizzle the schisandra berry sauce over the fried patties. Serve hot. - For the Schisandra Berry Sauce
